content.title: About
content.content: Bartlett pears are juicy, sweet fruits with a soft flesh and a thin edible skin. They are grown in temperate climates and are among the most popular pear varieties worldwide. Consumed fresh, they are also used in baking, desserts, and juices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Bartlett variety was developed in the United States in the early 19th century and named after John Bartlett, who first introduced it to America.
Pears belong to the Rosaceae family and are more closely related to apples than to other fruits.
The Bartlett harvest season typically runs from late summer to early autumn.
The skin is rich in antioxidants, while the flesh provides vitamin C, copper, and dietary fiber.
Pears can vary in shape and size depending on growing conditions and ripeness.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain gut health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids in blood pressure regulation and heart function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Pears are suitable for weight‑management diets due to their low calorie density.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to pears.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic fruit, wash thoroughly to remove possible chemical residues.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: High natural fructose content can cause discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pears can be eaten fresh, sliced into salads, added to yogurt, or used in compotes, jams, and baked dishes. For a softer texture, they can be gently warmed or roasted.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store pears in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, preferably in a separate bag or container. At room temperature they ripen quickly, so cooling extends their shelf life.
